literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒研究进展:从流行病学动态到疫苗开发新策略。
literature.lead_zh: 近期文献综述了汉坦病毒的流行病学变化、临床病理机制、生态风险以及针对新发暴发的疫苗开发前沿进展。
key_findings_zh: 汉坦病毒的流行病学格局正随气候变化、城市化及生态破坏而改变,且安第斯病毒已证实存在人传人传播风险 [10.1002/rmv.70191, 10.1016/j.clinpr.2026.100712]。
内皮功能障碍是汉坦病毒严重疾病的病理标志,而体外膜肺氧合 (ECMO) 可提高急性心肺综合征患者的生存率 [10.1002/rmv.70191]。
研究人员正通过免疫信息学设计针对保守糖蛋白的广谱多表位疫苗,旨在克服汉坦病毒物种间的高度变异性 [10.3390/ijms27157021]。
生态旅游的兴起增加了人类接触野生动物及其宿主环境的风险,可能成为汉坦病毒等人畜共患病暴发的新诱因 [10.1080/17460794.2026.2709930, 10.20944/preprints202608.0108.v1]。
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险趋势:气候变化与全球旅游业(尤其是生态旅游)增加了病毒跨物种传播的风险;临床上,由于缺乏特异性抗病毒药物,早期识别与支持性治疗至关重要。
literature.caveats_zh: 部分疫苗研究目前仅限于计算机模拟,尚需实验验证;部分流行病学观察具有定性性质,缺乏大规模定量数据。
literature.headline_en: Advances in Hantavirus Research: From Epidemiological Dynamics to Vaccine Strategies.
literature.lead_en: Recent literature reviews the changing epidemiology, clinical pathogenesis, ecological risks, and emerging vaccine development strategies for hantaviruses.
key_findings_en: The epidemiological landscape of hantaviruses is shifting due to climate change and urbanization, with evidence confirming person-to-person transmission of Andes virus [10.1002/rmv.70191, 10.1016/j.clinpr.2026.100712].
Endothelial dysfunction is the pathological hallmark of severe disease, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improves survival in fulminant HCPS [10.1002/rmv.70191].
Immunoinformatics-based multi-epitope vaccine designs targeting conserved glycoproteins show promise in overcoming high inter-species variability [10.3390/ijms27157021].
The rise of ecotourism increases human exposure to wildlife-associated environments, potentially facilitating zoonotic outbreaks [10.1080/17460794.2026.2709930, 10.20944/preprints202608.0108.v1].
literature.trend_or_risk_en: Risk Trend: Climate change and increased ecotourism elevate zoonotic spillover risks; clinically, the lack of specific antivirals necessitates early recognition and intensive supportive care.
literature.caveats_en: Some vaccine studies are limited to in silico simulations and require experimental validation; epidemiological observations are often qualitative.
literature.brief_en: Recent studies highlight the evolving epidemiological landscape of hantaviruses driven by environmental changes and ecotourism. Key clinical focus remains on supportive care like ECMO, while vaccine research shifts toward broad-spectrum multi-epitope designs to address viral diversity.

literature.zh: 近期文献综述了汉坦病毒的流行病学变化、临床病理机制、生态风险以及针对新发暴发的疫苗开发前沿进展。；汉坦病毒的流行病学格局正随气候变化、城市化及生态破坏而改变,且安第斯病毒已证实存在人传人传播风险 [10.1002/rmv.70191, 10.1016/j.clinpr.2026.100712]。；内皮功能障碍是汉坦病毒严重疾病的病理标志,而体外膜肺氧合 (ECMO) 可提高急性心肺综合征患者的生存率 [10.1002/rmv.70191]。；研究人员正通过免疫信息学设计针对保守糖蛋白的广谱多表位疫苗,旨在克服汉坦病毒物种间的高度变异性 [10.3390/ijms27157021]。；生态旅游的兴起增加了人类接触野生动物及其宿主环境的风险,可能成为汉坦病毒等人畜共患病暴发的新诱因 [10.1080/17460794.2026.2709930, 10.20944/preprints202608.0108.v1]。
literature.en: Recent literature reviews the changing epidemiology, clinical pathogenesis, ecological risks, and emerging vaccine development strategies for hantaviruses. The epidemiological landscape of hantaviruses is shifting due to climate change and urbanization, with evidence confirming person-to-person transmission of Andes virus [10.1002/rmv.70191, 10.1016/j.clinpr.2026.100712]. Endothelial dysfunction is the pathological hallmark of severe disease, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improves survival in fulminant HCPS [10.1002/rmv.70191]. Immunoinformatics-based multi-epitope vaccine designs targeting conserved glycoproteins show promise in overcoming high inter-species variability [10.3390/ijms27157021]. The rise of ecotourism increases human exposure to wildlife-associated environments, potentially facilitating zoonotic outbreaks [10.1080/17460794.2026.2709930, 10.20944/preprints202608.0108.v1].

papers.title: The Changing Landscape of Hantavirus Infections: A Narrative Review of Epidemiology, Pathogenesis, and Countermeasures.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are emerging zoonotic pathogens of increasing global public health significance. Their epidemiological landscape is rapidly changing due to ecological disruption, climate variability, urbanisation, and evolving human-animal interfaces. This narrative review synthesises current knowledge on hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management, and emerging countermeasures, with a focus on developments from the past 5 years. Traditionally classified into Old World viruses causing haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and New World viruses causing hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), this dichotomy has become increasingly blurred, with overlapping renal and pulmonary manifestations now recognized. Among the most consequential recent advances is the consolidated evidence for person-to-person transmission of Andes virus, documented among household contacts and during the prodromal phase, with viral shedding in respiratory secretions. Endothelial dysfunction remains the pathological hallmark of severe disease, driven by VEGF sensitisation, Src kinase and RhoA pathway activation, pericyte infection, and dysregulated inflammatory responses including IL-6 trans-signalling. Concurrently, environmental and ecological studies have linked climate change, rodent population dynamics, land-use modification, and urbanisation to increased human disease risk across multiple continents. Diagnostic strategies continue to rely on serology and molecular testing, while management remains predominantly supportive, with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improving survival in fulminant HCPS. Importantly, recent structural virology advances have enabled the development of broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies targeting conserved quaternary epitopes, as well as next-generation vaccine platforms including DNA, mRNA, and prefusion-stabilised glycoprotein candidates. Hantaviruses represent a paradigmatic One Health challenge at the intersection of environmental change, viral evolution, and global interconnectedness. Despite major progress in understanding transmission dynamics and endothelial pathogenesis, critical gaps remain regarding determinants of person-to-person spread, long-term post-infection sequelae, and the absence of licenced broadly protective vaccines or specific antiviral therapies. Future preparedness will require integrated surveillance frameworks combining ecological monitoring, genomic epidemiology, and clinical readiness within coordinated international public health strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review synthesises recent developments in hantavirus infections, focusing on mammalian orthohantaviruses (e.g., Hantaan, Seoul, Puumala, Dobrava-Belgrade, Sin Nombre, Andes viruses) and their associated human syndromes (HFRS, HCPS). Endothelial dysfunction underpins severe disease via VEGF sensitisation, Src/RhoA activation, pericyte infection, and IL-6 trans-signalling. Key gaps include unresolved determinants of person-to-person transmission, long-term sequelae, and the lack of licenced vaccines or antivirals. Preparedness demands integrated surveillance linking ecological, genomic, and clinical data.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 感染的变化格局:流行病学、发病机制 和对策的叙述回顾。
papers.source_body_en: Hantaviruses are emerging zoonotic pathogens of increasing global public health significance. Their epidemiological landscape is rapidly changing due to ecological disruption, climate variability, urbanisation, and evolving human-animal interfaces. This narrative review synthesises current knowledge on hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management, and emerging countermeasures, with a focus on developments from the past 5 years. Traditionally classified into Old World viruses causing haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and New World viruses causing hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), this dichotomy has become increasingly blurred, with overlapping renal and pulmonary manifestations now recognized. Among the most consequential recent advances is the consolidated evidence for person-to-person transmission of Andes virus, documented among household contacts and during the prodromal phase, with viral shedding in respiratory secretions. Endothelial dysfunction remains the pathological hallmark of severe disease, driven by VEGF sensitisation, Src kinase and RhoA pathway activation, pericyte infection, and dysregulated inflammatory responses including IL-6 trans-signalling. Concurrently, environmental and ecological studies have linked climate change, rodent population dynamics, land-use modification, and urbanisation to increased human disease risk across multiple continents. Diagnostic strategies continue to rely on serology and molecular testing, while management remains predominantly supportive, with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improving survival in fulminant HCPS. Importantly, recent structural virology advances have enabled the development of broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies targeting conserved quaternary epitopes, as well as next-generation vaccine platforms including DNA, mRNA, and prefusion-stabilised glycoprotein candidates. Hantaviruses represent a paradigmatic One Health challenge at the intersection of environmental change, viral evolution, and global interconnectedness. Despite major progress in understanding transmission dynamics and endothelial pathogenesis, critical gaps remain regarding determinants of person-to-person spread, long-term post-infection sequelae, and the absence of licenced broadly protective vaccines or specific antiviral therapies. Future preparedness will require integrated surveillance frameworks combining ecological monitoring, genomic epidemiology, and clinical readiness within coordinated international public health strategies.
papers.abstract_zh: 汉坦病毒 是新兴的人畜共患病原体,对全球公共卫生的重要性日益增加。由于生态破坏、气候变化、城市化和不断变化的人与动物界面,他们的流行病学格局正在迅速变化。这篇叙述性综述综合了汉坦病毒病毒学、流行病学、发病机制、临床管理和新兴对策的当前知识,重点关注过去 5 年的发展。传统上分为引起肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 的旧世界病毒和引起汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS) 的新世界病毒,这种二分法已变得越来越模糊,现在认识到肾脏和肺部表现重叠。最近最重要的进展之一是安第斯山脉病毒人传人 传播 的综合证据,记录在家庭接触者中和前驱阶段,病毒在呼吸道分泌物中脱落。内皮功能障碍仍然是严重疾病的病理标志,其驱动因素包括 VEGF 敏化、Src 激酶和 RhoA 通路激活、周细胞感染以及包括 IL-6 反式信号传导在内的炎症反应失调。与此同时,环境和生态研究将气候变化、啮齿动物种群动态、土地利用改变和城市化与多个大陆人类疾病风险的增加联系起来。诊断策略继续依赖 血清学 和分子检测,而管理仍然主要是支持性的,体外膜肺氧合 (ECMO) 可以提高暴发性 HCPS 的生存率。重要的是,最近的结构病毒学进展使得能够开发针对保守四级表位的广泛中和单克隆抗体,以及下一代 疫苗 平台,包括 DNA、mRNA 和融合前稳定的糖蛋白候选物。汉坦病毒代表了环境变化、病毒 进化 和全球互联性交叉点的典型“同一个健康”挑战。尽管在了解 传播 动力学和内皮 发病机制 方面取得了重大进展,但在人与人之间传播的决定因素、长期感染后后遗症以及缺乏获得许可的广泛保护性 疫苗 或特定 抗病毒药物 疗法方面仍然存在关键差距。未来的准备将需要综合的 监测 框架,将生态监测、基因组 流行病学 和协调国际公共卫生战略中的临床准备结合起来。

papers.title: Cruise-linked Andes virus and severe hantavirus lung disease: A narrative review
papers.abstract: The 2026 cruise-linked Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak represents a rare but high-consequence travel-associated zoonotic event, combining likely land-based acquisition before embarkation, limited onboard human-to-human transmission, delayed clinical recognition, and multinational public health coordination. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the outbreak, ANDV biology, transmission dynamics, clinical presentation, diagnostics, management, and implications for maritime and expedition travel medicine. As of 2 July 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) had reported 13 cases linked to the motor vessel (M/V) Hondius outbreak, including 12 laboratory-confirmed infections, one probable case, and three deaths. Following completion of the 42-day follow-up period for all identified contacts without additional secondary cases, WHO considered transmission interrupted and the outbreak contained. Available evidence supports likely land-based acquisition before embarkation followed by limited onboard human-to-human transmission, without sustained spread. Severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome may begin with nonspecific fever, malaise, myalgia, gastrointestinal symptoms, or respiratory complaints, then progress abruptly to pulmonary oedema, shock, and fatal cardiopulmonary collapse. Because no licensed antiviral therapy or vaccine is available, early recognition, cautious fluid management, intensive supportive care, ventilatory support, and timely transfer to intensive care or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-capable centres remain central. The outbreak highlights critical preparedness gaps in shipboard triage, contact tracing, specimen transport, genomic surveillance, risk communication, and cross-border follow-up. Strengthening One Health-informed pre-travel counseling, post-travel symptom surveillance, and maritime outbreak protocols is essential for future expedition-associated zoonotic threats.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review examines the 2026 cruise-linked Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak, highlighting its rare but high-consequence nature as a travel-associated zoonotic event. The review outlines the likely transmission pathway, involving land-based acquisition before embarkation and limited onboard human-to-human spread, with no sustained transmission. It underscores the importance of early recognition, cautious fluid management, and intensive supportive care for managing severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). The outbreak also reveals critical preparedness gaps in maritime public health protocols, including shipboard triage, contact tracing, and genomic surveillance. The review calls for enhanced One Health-informed strategies for pre-travel counseling, post-travel symptom monitoring, and outbreak response to mitigate future risks of hantavirus-related zoonotic threats.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注与邮轮相关的安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 暴发 和严重的汉坦病毒肺部疾病,检查病原体、其相关综合征以及对海上旅行医学的影响。核心问题是 ANDV 如何在旅行相关环境中传播以及汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS) 的临床结果。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 ANDV 生物学、传播 动力学、临床表现、诊断、管理和 暴发 影响的当前证据的叙述性综合。它不报告具体的数据库、检索日期或荟萃分析方法,而是依赖专家意见和现有文献。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,M/V Hondius 上的 2026 ANDV 暴发 可能涉及登船前的陆基传播、有限的船上人际传播 传播,且没有持续传播。世卫组织在 42 天的随访期后宣布 暴发 已得到控制,没有出现其他继发病例。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,暴发 强调了船上分类、接触者追踪和 基因组监测 方面的差距。没有明确提及 传播 动态或 ANDV 临床管理中相互矛盾的发现或证据差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调需要加强 One Health 旅行前咨询、旅行后症状 监测 和海上 暴发 协议,以应对未来与汉坦病毒相关的人畜共患威胁。

papers.title: Hantavirus Infections in Children.
papers.abstract: Abstract Hantaviruses are rare but deadly pathogens. New World hantaviruses, primarily present in North and South America, cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which leads to death in up to one-third of affected patients. Old World hantaviruses, primarily endemic to Europe and Asia, cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and, dependent on the specific hantavirus, may cause death in up to 15% of patients. A heightened clinical suspicion is important for diagnosis of these conditions because important epidemiologic clues may exist at the time of presentation. A variety of testing modalities exist, from evaluation of blood smears (for hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome and may be available at many rural clinics) to serological evaluation and polymerase chain reaction testing (available at tertiary care centers or as a send-out to a reference laboratory). Despite the absence of proven antiviral therapies for many of these viruses, supportive care present at tertiary-level medical centers including invasive cardiovascular monitoring, mechanical ventilation, and access to dialysis (for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome) and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (for hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome) may improve outcomes. Given the high risk of death as well as the potential for these patients to decompensate rapidly over 24 hours, early recognition of hantavirus infections and transfer to a tertiary medical center is imperative. The nonspecific prodrome, which mimics more common viral illnesses ubiquitous in children, as well as a more rapid progression to death in children than adults with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, highlights the need for pediatricians to remain vigilant for this rare and dangerous disease.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human hantavirus infections in children, focusing on orthohantaviruses associated with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), their geographic distribution, clinical severity, and diagnostic challenges. The central question addresses the recognition, clinical course, and management priorities for these rare but life-threatening pediatric infections.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis without explicit systematic review methods, databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study selection procedures reported. It synthesizes general knowledge about hantavirus syndromes and their clinical management without detailing inclusion criteria or meta-analytic processes.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Old World hantaviruses cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome with mortality up to 15%, while New World hantaviruses cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome with mortality up to one-third of patients. Early recognition and transfer to tertiary care are critical due to rapid clinical deterioration, particularly in children who may decompensate faster than adults.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report specific diagnostic test performance metrics, antiviral efficacy data, or comparative effectiveness of supportive care modalities. It also does not address pediatric-specific seroprevalence data, age-stratified risk factors, or long-term outcomes beyond acute illness.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Pediatricians should maintain high clinical suspicion for hantavirus infections given nonspecific prodromes and rapid progression, especially in endemic regions. Improved access to rapid diagnostic testing and standardized pediatric-specific management protocols, including invasive monitoring and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, may reduce mortality.

analysis.summary_en: This review highlights hantavirus infections in children as rare but severe, with Old World hantaviruses causing hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (up to 15% mortality) and New World hantaviruses causing hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (up to one-third mortality). Early clinical recognition is critical due to rapid deterioration, particularly in pediatric patients who may decompensate faster than adults. Diagnostic modalities range from blood smears in rural settings to serology and PCR in tertiary centers. Supportive care, including invasive monitoring, mechanical ventilation, dialysis, and ECMO, may improve outcomes despite the absence of proven antivirals. The review underscores the need for heightened pediatric vigilance and timely transfer to tertiary care.

elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis without explicit systematic review methods, databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study selection procedures reported. It synthesizes general knowledge about hantavirus syndromes and their clinical management without detailing inclusion criteria or meta-analytic processes.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Old World hantaviruses cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome with mortality up to 15%, while New World hantaviruses cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome with mortality up to one-third of patients. Early recognition and transfer to tertiary care are critical due to rapid clinical deterioration, particularly in children who may decompensate faster than adults.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report specific diagnostic test performance metrics, antiviral efficacy data, or comparative effectiveness of supportive care modalities. It also does not address pediatric-specific seroprevalence data, age-stratified risk factors, or long-term outcomes beyond acute illness.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: Pediatricians should maintain high clinical suspicion for hantavirus infections given nonspecific prodromes and rapid progression, especially in endemic regions. Improved access to rapid diagnostic testing and standardized pediatric-specific management protocols, including invasive monitoring and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, may reduce mortality.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 旧世界汉坦病毒导致肾综合征出血热和死亡率高达15%,而新世界汉坦病毒导致汉坦病毒心肺综合征和死亡率高达三分之一的患者。由于临床病情迅速恶化,早期识别并转移至三级护理至关重要,特别是对于可能比成人更快失代偿的儿童。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告具体的诊断测试性能指标、抗病毒药物 疗效数据或支持性护理方式的比较有效性。它还不涉及儿科特定的 血清流行率 数据、年龄分层的危险因素或急性疾病以外的长期结果。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 鉴于非特异性前驱症状和快速进展,特别是在流行地区,儿科医生应保持对汉坦病毒感染的高度临床怀疑。改进快速诊断测试和标准化儿科特定管理方案(包括侵入性监测和体外膜氧合)可能会减少 死亡率。

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 儿童感染。
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Hantaviruses are rare but deadly pathogens. New World hantaviruses, primarily present in North and South America, cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which leads to death in up to one-third of affected patients. Old World hantaviruses, primarily endemic to Europe and Asia, cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and, dependent on the specific hantavirus, may cause death in up to 15% of patients. A heightened clinical suspicion is important for diagnosis of these conditions because important epidemiologic clues may exist at the time of presentation. A variety of testing modalities exist, from evaluation of blood smears (for hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome and may be available at many rural clinics) to serological evaluation and polymerase chain reaction testing (available at tertiary care centers or as a send-out to a reference laboratory). Despite the absence of proven antiviral therapies for many of these viruses, supportive care present at tertiary-level medical centers including invasive cardiovascular monitoring, mechanical ventilation, and access to dialysis (for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome) and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (for hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome) may improve outcomes. Given the high risk of death as well as the potential for these patients to decompensate rapidly over 24 hours, early recognition of hantavirus infections and transfer to a tertiary medical center is imperative. The nonspecific prodrome, which mimics more common viral illnesses ubiquitous in children, as well as a more rapid progression to death in children than adults with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, highlights the need for pediatricians to remain vigilant for this rare and dangerous disease.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要汉坦病毒是罕见但致命的病原体。新世界汉坦病毒主要存在于北美和南美,会引起汉坦病毒心肺综合征,导致多达三分之一的受影响患者死亡。旧世界汉坦病毒主要流行于欧洲和亚洲,导致 肾综合征出血热,并且根据特定的 汉坦病毒,可能导致高达 15% 的患者死亡。对于 诊断 来说,高度临床怀疑对这些病症很重要,因为在发病时可能存在重要的流行病学线索。存在多种检测方式,从血涂片评估(针对汉坦病毒心肺综合征,许多农村诊所均可提供)到血清学评估和聚合酶链反应检测(三级护理中心可提供或发送到参考实验室)。尽管对于许多此类病毒缺乏经过验证的 抗病毒药物 疗法,但三级医疗中心提供的支持性护理,包括侵入性心血管监测、机械通气、透析(针对 肾综合征出血热)和体外膜氧合(针对汉坦病毒心肺综合征)可能会改善预后。鉴于死亡风险较高以及这些患者可能在 24 小时内迅速失代偿,因此必须及早识别汉坦病毒感染并转移至三级医疗中心。这种非特异性前驱症状类似于儿童中普遍存在的更常见的病毒性疾病,并且汉坦病毒心肺综合征儿童比成人更快地进展至死亡,这凸显了儿科医生需要对这种罕见而危险的疾病保持警惕。

papers.title: Revisiting Animal Reservoirs of Hantavirus and Other Zoonotic Viruses on Cruise Ships: Impact and Prevention
papers.abstract: The sustained growth of international maritime tourism and the expansion of the cruise industry have increased the importance of emerging zoonotic diseases as a significant challenge to global public health. Cruise ships constitute complex epidemiological settings characterized by high population density, rapid international mobility, and constant interaction between humans, animals, and coastal environments, factors that favor the introduction and spread of emerging infectious agents. Among the main threats are hantaviruses and other zoonotic viruses, such as dengue, chikungunya, Zika, yellow fever, and avian influenza, which are associated with animal reservoirs and vectors present in ports, tourist destinations, and tropical ecosystems. This review examines the ecology of animal reservoirs of hantaviruses and other zoonotic pathogens relevant to maritime tourism, including peri-urban rodents, bats, migratory birds, and other mammals. It discusses the impact of climate change, coastal urbanization, and environmental change on viral transmission dynamics. Epidemiological risks linked to international cruises are highlighted, particularly exposure during ecotourism excursions, pathogen introduction, and challenges for maritime surveillance. The review also addresses travel medicine, biosecurity, and infection control, emphasizing a One Health approach. Strengthening integrated surveillance and prevention systems is essential to ensure safer, more sustainable, and resilient maritime tourism in the 21st century.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本次审查重点关注汉坦病毒及其相关综合症,特别是在游轮和海上旅游的背景下。它阐述了动物 储存宿主 在汉坦病毒和其他人畜共患病毒的 传播 中的作用,并评估这些病毒在此类环境中对人类健康的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一份预印本,研究了汉坦病毒的动物 储存宿主 和与海上旅游相关的其他人畜共患病原体的生态学。它包括对与国际邮轮相关的流行病学风险的讨论,特别是生态旅游游览期间的暴露、病原体的引入以及海上 监测 的挑战。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该评论强调了汉坦病毒和其他人畜共患病毒在游轮中的重要性,强调了城市周边啮齿动物、蝙蝠、候鸟和其他哺乳动物作为潜在 储存宿主 的作用。它还讨论了气候变化、沿海城市化和环境变化对病毒 传播 动态的影响。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,与国际邮轮相关的流行病学风险尚未完全了解,特别是关于游轮上汉坦病毒传播 的具体机制。目前缺乏关于不同动物 储存宿主 在病毒传播中的作用以及当前预防策略有效性的详细数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查表明,加强综合 监测 和预防系统对于确保 21 世纪的海上​​旅游业更安全、更可持续和更有弹性至关重要。它还强调需要采用“同一个健康”方法来解决人类、动物和环境健康之间复杂的相互作用。

analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the epidemiological risks linked to international cruises are not fully understood, particularly regarding the specific mechanisms of hantavirus transmission on cruise ships. There is a lack of detailed data on the role of different animal reservoirs in viral spread and the effectiveness of current prevention strategies.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that strengthening integrated surveillance and prevention systems is essential to ensure safer, more sustainable, and resilient maritime tourism in the 21st century. It also emphasizes the need for a One Health approach to address the complex interactions between human, animal, and environmental health.

papers.title_zh: 重温汉坦病毒和其他人畜共患病毒对游轮的动物储存宿主:影响和预防
papers.source_body_en: The sustained growth of international maritime tourism and the expansion of the cruise industry have increased the importance of emerging zoonotic diseases as a significant challenge to global public health. Cruise ships constitute complex epidemiological settings characterized by high population density, rapid international mobility, and constant interaction between humans, animals, and coastal environments, factors that favor the introduction and spread of emerging infectious agents. Among the main threats are hantaviruses and other zoonotic viruses, such as dengue, chikungunya, Zika, yellow fever, and avian influenza, which are associated with animal reservoirs and vectors present in ports, tourist destinations, and tropical ecosystems. This review examines the ecology of animal reservoirs of hantaviruses and other zoonotic pathogens relevant to maritime tourism, including peri-urban rodents, bats, migratory birds, and other mammals. It discusses the impact of climate change, coastal urbanization, and environmental change on viral transmission dynamics. Epidemiological risks linked to international cruises are highlighted, particularly exposure during ecotourism excursions, pathogen introduction, and challenges for maritime surveillance. The review also addresses travel medicine, biosecurity, and infection control, emphasizing a One Health approach. Strengthening integrated surveillance and prevention systems is essential to ensure safer, more sustainable, and resilient maritime tourism in the 21st century.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本次审查重点关注汉坦病毒及其相关综合症,特别是在游轮和海上旅游的背景下。它阐述了动物 储存宿主 在汉坦病毒和其他人畜共患病毒的 传播 中的作用,并评估这些病毒在此类环境中对人类健康的影响。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一份预印本,研究了汉坦病毒的动物 储存宿主 和与海上旅游相关的其他人畜共患病原体的生态学。它包括对与国际邮轮相关的流行病学风险的讨论,特别是生态旅游游览期间的暴露、病原体的引入以及海上 监测 的挑战。

papers.title: Rapid response and surveillance for high-risk contacts during May 2026 Andes hantavirus outbreak: a Northern Italy experience
papers.abstract: In May 2026, an outbreak of Andes hantavirus (ANDV) linked to the cruise ship MV Hondius prompted international contact tracing across multiple countries. Although population-level risk was low, the severity of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome and limited evidence on person-to-person transmission supported precautionary management of selected contacts. Lombardy Region, Northern Italy, was notified of a contact-tracing chain involving four individuals: two direct flight-related contacts exposed to confirmed ANDV cases during international air travel and their two accompanying close contacts. A coordinated response was activated through regional, national, and international public health authorities. All four were referred to Luigi Sacco University Hospital and managed under precautionary measures proportionate to their exposure category. RT-PCR testing for ANDV was negative in all four. This experience illustrates how imported pathogens may generate complex regional demands even when population-level risk remains low, and underscores the value of predefined preparedness frameworks.

papers.source_body_en: In May 2026, an outbreak of Andes hantavirus (ANDV) linked to the cruise ship MV Hondius prompted international contact tracing across multiple countries. Although population-level risk was low, the severity of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome and limited evidence on person-to-person transmission supported precautionary management of selected contacts. Lombardy Region, Northern Italy, was notified of a contact-tracing chain involving four individuals: two direct flight-related contacts exposed to confirmed ANDV cases during international air travel and their two accompanying close contacts. A coordinated response was activated through regional, national, and international public health authorities. All four were referred to Luigi Sacco University Hospital and managed under precautionary measures proportionate to their exposure category. RT-PCR testing for ANDV was negative in all four. This experience illustrates how imported pathogens may generate complex regional demands even when population-level risk remains low, and underscores the value of predefined preparedness frameworks.

papers.title: Broad-Spectrum Multi-Epitope Design Targeting Conserved Hantavirus Glycoproteins (Gn/Gc): Chimeric Antigen Engineering and Structural Mapping
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses, the etiological agents of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), represent a high-risk zoonotic threat with substantial global health impact. Currently, there is no FDA-approved vaccine. The viral surface glycoprotein (GP) is crucial for host cell entry and is regarded as a key target for vaccine development. However, its variability among hantavirus species limits the effectiveness of conventional vaccine strategies. Epitope-based vaccines offer a promising alternative by enabling the design of broadly protective constructs. In this study, we applied immunoinformatics approaches to design a universal multi-epitope vaccine candidate targeting both HFRS- and HPS-associated hantaviruses through a multi-layered workflow integrating B-cell and T-cell epitope prediction, antigenicity scoring, IFN-γ induction potential, conservation analysis, and population coverage assessment. Viral GPs from SEOV, PUUV, SNV, and ANDV were analyzed using algorithms for B-cell and T-cell epitope prediction. Predicted epitopes were assessed for allergenicity, toxicity, conservation, and population coverage. Two vaccine constructs incorporating β-defensin or 50S ribosomal protein L7/L12 as adjuvants were assessed for physicochemical properties, structural stability and immunogenic potential. Molecular docking analyses provided exploratory ectodomain-compatibility screening, suggesting potential interactions with TLR4 that require future experimental confirmation. The in silico immune simulations suggested potential robust and long-lasting responses with memory cell persistence exceeding one year. Simulations also indicated balanced humoral and cellular responses, robust antibody production, and long-term memory formation suggestive of durable protective immunity. These findings support the rational design of broad-spectrum multi-epitope vaccines against genetically diverse hantaviruses, offering a rational framework for preclinical development of next-generation universal vaccines against hantavirus-associated diseases.

papers.title_zh: 针对保守汉坦病毒糖蛋白 (Gn/Gc) 的广谱多表位设计:嵌合抗原工程和结构作图
papers.source_body_en: Hantaviruses, the etiological agents of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), represent a high-risk zoonotic threat with substantial global health impact. Currently, there is no FDA-approved vaccine. The viral surface glycoprotein (GP) is crucial for host cell entry and is regarded as a key target for vaccine development. However, its variability among hantavirus species limits the effectiveness of conventional vaccine strategies. Epitope-based vaccines offer a promising alternative by enabling the design of broadly protective constructs. In this study, we applied immunoinformatics approaches to design a universal multi-epitope vaccine candidate targeting both HFRS- and HPS-associated hantaviruses through a multi-layered workflow integrating B-cell and T-cell epitope prediction, antigenicity scoring, IFN-γ induction potential, conservation analysis, and population coverage assessment. Viral GPs from SEOV, PUUV, SNV, and ANDV were analyzed using algorithms for B-cell and T-cell epitope prediction. Predicted epitopes were assessed for allergenicity, toxicity, conservation, and population coverage. Two vaccine constructs incorporating β-defensin or 50S ribosomal protein L7/L12 as adjuvants were assessed for physicochemical properties, structural stability and immunogenic potential. Molecular docking analyses provided exploratory ectodomain-compatibility screening, suggesting potential interactions with TLR4 that require future experimental confirmation. The in silico immune simulations suggested potential robust and long-lasting responses with memory cell persistence exceeding one year. Simulations also indicated balanced humoral and cellular responses, robust antibody production, and long-term memory formation suggestive of durable protective immunity. These findings support the rational design of broad-spectrum multi-epitope vaccines against genetically diverse hantaviruses, offering a rational framework for preclinical development of next-generation universal vaccines against hantavirus-associated diseases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to address the growing concern about hantavirus transmission risks associated with ecotourism and to understand how travel can increase human exposure to wildlife-associated environments. The paper asks how the increasing popularity of expedition cruises may influence the spread of hantaviruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is an editorial analysis of a hantavirus outbreak linked to the MV Hondius expedition cruise ship, focusing on the context of ecotourism. It examines the risk of zoonotic disease transmission in such settings and considers the specific syndromes associated with hantavirus infections.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a review of the outbreak's epidemiological context, including the environmental and behavioral factors that may have contributed to the transmission of hantaviruses during the cruise. The analysis is based on reported cases and environmental data.
analysis.main_results: The outbreak on the MV Hondius demonstrated that hantavirus can be transmitted through exposure to rodent-infested environments on cruise ships, highlighting the potential for ecotourism to facilitate zoonotic disease spread.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that ecotourism can increase the risk of hantavirus transmission by bringing humans into contact with wildlife-associated environments. This is a novel perspective on the role of travel in zoonotic disease dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform public health strategies for monitoring and preventing hantavirus outbreaks in ecotourism settings, emphasizing the need for improved environmental and health protocols on cruise ships.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an editorial analysis of a single outbreak, which may not be representative of all hantavirus transmission scenarios. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the lack of quantitative data and controlled experiments.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial explores the risk of hantavirus transmission in ecotourism settings, focusing on the outbreak associated with the MV Hondius cruise ship. It highlights how travel can increase human exposure to wildlife-associated environments, potentially facilitating zoonotic disease spread. The study suggests that ecotourism may play a role in the emergence of hantavirus infections and calls for improved surveillance and prevention measures in such contexts. While the analysis is based on a single event, it provides a novel perspective on the intersection of travel, ecology, and public health. The findings are relevant for understanding the broader implications of human-wildlife interactions in the context of global travel trends.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对与 MV Hondius 探险游轮相关的汉坦病毒暴发 的编辑分析,重点关注生态旅游的背景。它检查了此类环境中人畜共患疾病 传播 的风险,并考虑了与汉坦病毒感染相关的特定综合征。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及对 暴发 的流行病学背景进行审查,包括在巡航期间可能导致 传播 的环境和行为因素。该分析基于报告的案例和环境数据。
elements_zh.main_results: MV Hondius 上的 暴发 证明,汉坦病毒 可以通过游轮上啮齿动物出没的环境传播,这凸显了生态旅游促进人畜共患疾病传播的潜力。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为生态旅游可以通过使人类接触与野生动物相关的环境来增加汉坦病毒传播 风险的证据。这是关于旅行在人畜共患疾病动态中的作用的新视角。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为生态旅游环境中监测和预防汉坦病毒暴发 的公共卫生策略提供了信息,强调需要改进游轮上的环境和健康协议。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于对单个 暴发 的编辑分析,可能无法代表所有汉坦病毒传播 场景。由于缺乏定量数据和对照实验,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Emerging infectious diseases (Mpox, Nipah, and Andes): A narrative review of transmission, environmental survival, and disinfection.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus are emerging infectious diseases that cause outbreaks associated with nosocomial transmission. METHODS: This narrative review summarizes the Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment with a focus on environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention. RESULTS: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus all survive in the environment and are capable of indirect transmission. All these viruses are enveloped and susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants. CONCLUSIONS: Rapid identification of patients with known or suspected infections of these emerging viruses coupled with adherence to infection prevention recommendations will prevent healthcare-associated transmission.

papers.title: We trained for medicine, not for this: how young doctors should (not) address outbreaks after COVID-19
papers.abstract: The authors reflect on how young physicians navigate emerging infectious disease outbreaks in the post-COVID era, using the 2026 multi-country hantavirus clusters and the concurrent Ebola Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) as catalysts for discussing professional identity, communication, adaptability and preparedness among younger generations of doctors. Reports of hantavirus clusters linked to international travel and possible human-to-human transmission involving the Andes hantavirus strain emerged in parallel with the declaration of a WHO PHEIC related to Bundibugyo ebolavirus cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. These events revived what may be described as ‘outbreak memory’: the lingering professional, psychological and communicational imprint left by previous epidemics, particularly COVID-19. Young physicians occupy a uniquely exposed position within this environment, having completed medical school or residency during periods marked by redeployment, disrupted training, workforce shortages, emotional exhaustion, digital hyperconnectivity and growing expectations for public communication. Drawing on lived experiences from the COVID-19 era, this viewpoint presents seven thematic reflections for young physicians addressing pandemic framing, patient-centredness, adaptability across specialties, communication and media engagement, professional conduct online, workplace hierarchy and teamwork during emerging outbreaks. Future outbreaks will continue to test not only healthcare systems but also the professional identities and communication practices of younger generations of physicians. Preparedness after COVID-19 is no longer solely about protocols and biomedical response capacity. It also requires supporting young physicians in learning how to remain clinically grounded, collaborative, adaptable and professionally responsible while practising medicine in a context of uncertainty.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors present a viewpoint based on thematic reflections drawn from lived experiences during the COVID-19 era, focusing on the professional challenges faced by young physicians navigating outbreaks such as hantavirus clusters and Ebola PHEIC.
analysis.methods: The paper synthesizes qualitative reflections on professional conduct, communication, adaptability, and teamwork during outbreaks, integrating observations from the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent emerging infectious disease events.
analysis.main_results: The authors identify seven thematic reflections for young physicians addressing pandemic framing, patient-centredness, cross-specialty adaptability, communication and media engagement, professional conduct online, workplace hierarchy, and teamwork during emerging outbreaks.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets the findings as evidence that preparedness for future outbreaks requires more than protocols and biomedical capacity, emphasizing the need to support young physicians in maintaining clinical grounding, collaboration, adaptability, and professional responsibility amid uncertainty.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening the professional resilience and communication skills of young physicians is critical for effective outbreak response and public health communication in contexts of uncertainty and evolving threats.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is qualitative and viewpoint-based, lacking empirical data or direct measurements of outbreak responses, which limits generalizability and strength to a moderate level.

analysis.summary_en: This viewpoint paper explores how young physicians navigate emerging infectious disease outbreaks in the post-COVID era, using recent hantavirus clusters and an Ebola Public Health Emergency of International Concern as illustrative cases. The authors argue that preparedness for future outbreaks extends beyond protocols and biomedical capacity, requiring support for young doctors to remain clinically grounded, collaborative, adaptable, and professionally responsible amid uncertainty. Seven thematic reflections are presented, addressing pandemic framing, patient-centredness, cross-specialty adaptability, communication and media engagement, professional conduct online, workplace hierarchy, and teamwork. The study interprets these reflections as evidence that professional identity and communication practices are central to effective outbreak response. While the qualitative insights are valuable, the lack of empirical data limits the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis_en.methods: The paper synthesizes qualitative reflections on professional conduct, communication, adaptability, and teamwork during outbreaks, integrating observations from the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent emerging infectious disease events.
analysis_en.main_results: The authors identify seven thematic reflections for young physicians addressing pandemic framing, patient-centredness, cross-specialty adaptability, communication and media engagement, professional conduct online, workplace hierarchy, and teamwork during emerging outbreaks.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets the findings as evidence that preparedness for future outbreaks requires more than protocols and biomedical capacity, emphasizing the need to support young physicians in maintaining clinical grounding, collaboration, adaptability, and professional responsibility amid uncertainty.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening the professional resilience and communication skills of young physicians is critical for effective outbreak response and public health communication in contexts of uncertainty and evolving threats.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is qualitative and viewpoint-based, lacking empirical data or direct measurements of outbreak responses, which limits generalizability and strength to a moderate level.

papers.title_zh: 我们接受医学培训,而不是为此:年轻医生在 COVID-19 后应该(不)如何解决 暴发
papers.source_body_en: The authors reflect on how young physicians navigate emerging infectious disease outbreaks in the post-COVID era, using the 2026 multi-country hantavirus clusters and the concurrent Ebola Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) as catalysts for discussing professional identity, communication, adaptability and preparedness among younger generations of doctors. Reports of hantavirus clusters linked to international travel and possible human-to-human transmission involving the Andes hantavirus strain emerged in parallel with the declaration of a WHO PHEIC related to Bundibugyo ebolavirus cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. These events revived what may be described as ‘outbreak memory’: the lingering professional, psychological and communicational imprint left by previous epidemics, particularly COVID-19. Young physicians occupy a uniquely exposed position within this environment, having completed medical school or residency during periods marked by redeployment, disrupted training, workforce shortages, emotional exhaustion, digital hyperconnectivity and growing expectations for public communication. Drawing on lived experiences from the COVID-19 era, this viewpoint presents seven thematic reflections for young physicians addressing pandemic framing, patient-centredness, adaptability across specialties, communication and media engagement, professional conduct online, workplace hierarchy and teamwork during emerging outbreaks. Future outbreaks will continue to test not only healthcare systems but also the professional identities and communication practices of younger generations of physicians. Preparedness after COVID-19 is no longer solely about protocols and biomedical response capacity. It also requires supporting young physicians in learning how to remain clinically grounded, collaborative, adaptable and professionally responsible while practising medicine in a context of uncertainty.

papers.title: A streamlined visual RT-RAA-CRISPR/Cas12a assay for rapid detection of Schmallenberg virus
papers.abstract: Abstract Schmallenberg virus (SBV), an emerging Culicoides‐borne arbovirus, is responsible for febrile illness and reduced milk production in adult ruminants and can induce congenital malformations in fetuses, representing a substantial concern for livestock health worldwide. Consequently, rapid, field‐adaptable diagnostic approaches are urgently needed. In this study, we developed a visual nucleic acid detection assay for SBV that combines reverse transcription recombinase‐aided amplification (RT‐RAA) with the CRISPR/Cas12a system, targeting conserved regions of the SBV S gene. Following systematic optimization of the reaction conditions, the assay was completed within 50 min, with a sensitivity of 8.6 copies/μL for the SBV- S plasmid and 8.6 × 10 1 copies/μL for the RNA transcripts. The assay exhibited high specificity, with no cross‐reactivity observed against a panel of relevant pathogens, including Seoul orthohantavirus (SEOV), infectious bovine rhinotracheitis virus (IBRV), Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV), Crimean‐Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), and bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV). When evaluated using simulated clinical samples, the sensitivity of the method was superior to that of conventional real-time fluorescent reverse transcription‒polymerase chain reaction (RT‐qPCR). Importantly, the entire reaction is performed in a single closed-tube format, significantly reducing the risk of cross-contamination and false-positive results. In summary, this method demonstrates favorable analytical performance for the detection of SBV- S plasmid-spiked nasal swab samples and holds promise for further clinical validation, although its diagnostic utility in authentic clinical specimens remains to be confirmed in future investigations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Schmallenberg virus (SBV) causes febrile illness, reduced milk production in adult ruminants, and congenital malformations in fetuses, posing a substantial global threat to livestock health. Rapid, field-adaptable diagnostic approaches are urgently needed to address this emerging arboviral disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a visual nucleic acid detection assay for SBV by combining reverse transcription recombinase-aided amplification (RT-RAA) with the CRISPR/Cas12a system, targeting conserved regions of the SBV S gene. The assay was optimized and evaluated using plasmid and RNA transcript standards, as well as simulated clinical samples.
analysis.methods: The assay targeted conserved regions of the SBV S gene and was optimized for reaction conditions to complete within 50 minutes. Sensitivity was determined as 8.6 copies/μL for the SBV-S plasmid and 8.6 × 10^1 copies/μL for RNA transcripts. Specificity was assessed against a panel including Seoul orthohantavirus (SEOV), infectious bovine rhinotracheitis virus (IBRV), Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), and bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV), with no cross-reactivity observed.
analysis.main_results: The assay achieved a sensitivity of 8.6 copies/μL for the SBV-S plasmid and 8.6 × 10^1 copies/μL for RNA transcripts, with no cross-reactivity against the tested panel of pathogens. In simulated clinical samples, the assay's sensitivity exceeded that of conventional RT-qPCR.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the assay as demonstrating favorable analytical performance for SBV detection, highlighting its single closed-tube format that reduces cross-contamination risk. The novelty lies in the streamlined integration of RT-RAA with CRISPR/Cas12a for rapid, visual detection of SBV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This assay could enable rapid, field-deployable SBV detection, supporting livestock disease surveillance and outbreak response. Its closed-tube format and superior sensitivity to RT-qPCR suggest potential for improved diagnostic workflows in resource-limited settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report diagnostic validation in authentic clinical specimens, limiting immediate clinical applicability. While analytical performance is strong, the absence of field testing reduces the evidence strength to moderate until further validation is completed.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a rapid, visual RT-RAA-CRISPR/Cas12a assay for detecting Schmallenberg virus (SBV) by targeting conserved regions of the SBV S gene. The assay completed within 50 minutes with high sensitivity (8.6 copies/μL for plasmid, 8.6 × 10^1 copies/μL for RNA transcripts) and specificity, showing no cross-reactivity against a panel including Seoul orthohantavirus and other pathogens. In simulated clinical samples, sensitivity surpassed conventional RT-qPCR. The single closed-tube format minimizes cross-contamination risk. However, diagnostic utility in authentic clinical specimens remains unconfirmed, and further validation is required before clinical deployment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 施马伦贝格病毒 (SBV) 会导致发热性疾病、成年反刍动物产奶量减少以及胎儿先天畸形,对全球牲畜健康构成重大威胁。迫切需要快速、适用于现场的诊断方法来解决这种新出现的虫媒病毒疾病。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究通过将逆转录重组酶辅助扩增 (RT-RAA) 与 CRISPR/Cas12a 系统相结合,开发了一种 SBV 可视化核酸检测方法,针对 SBV S 基因的保守区域。使用质粒和 RNA 转录标准品以及模拟临床样本对该测定进行了优化和评估。
elements_zh.methods: 该测定针对 SBV S 基因的保守区域,并针对反应条件进行了优化,可在 50 分钟内完成。SBV-S 质粒的灵敏度确定为 8.6 拷贝/μL,RNA 转录本的灵敏度确定为 8.6 × 10^1 拷贝/μL。针对首尔正汉坦病毒 (SEOV)、传染性牛鼻气管炎病毒 (IBRV)、裂谷热病毒 (RVFV)、克里米亚-刚果出血热病毒 (CCHFV) 和牛病毒性腹泻病毒 (BVDV) 等一组病毒进行特异性评估,未观察到交叉反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 该测定对 SBV-S 质粒的灵敏度为 8.6 拷贝/μL,对 RNA 转录本的灵敏度为 8.6 × 10^1 拷贝/μL,并且与测试的病原体组没有交叉反应。在模拟临床样本中,该检测的灵敏度超过了传统 RT-qPCR。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将该测定解释为证明了 SBV 检测的良好分析性能,强调其单一闭管形式可降低交叉污染风险。新颖之处在于 RT-RAA 与 CRISPR/Cas12a 的简化集成,可快速、直观地检测 SBV。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该测定可以实现快速、可现场部署的 SBV 检测,支持牲畜疾病 监测 和 暴发 应对。其闭管形式和对 RT-qPCR 的卓越敏感性表明在资源有限的环境中改善诊断工作流程的潜力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告真实临床标本的诊断验证,限制了直接的临床适用性。虽然分析性能很强,但缺乏现场测试会导致证据强度中等,直到完成进一步验证。

When evaluated using simulated clinical samples, the sensitivity of the method was superior to that of conventional real-time fluorescent reverse transcription‒polymerase chain reaction (RT‐qPCR). Importantly, the entire reaction is performed in a single closed-tube format, significantly reducing the risk of cross-contamination and false-positive results. In summary, this method demonstrates favorable analytical performance for the detection of SBV- S plasmid-spiked nasal swab samples and holds promise for further clinical validation, although its diagnostic utility in authentic clinical specimens remains to be confirmed in future investigations.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 Schmallenberg 病毒 (SBV) 是一种新出现的库蠓传播的虫媒病毒,可导致成年反刍动物发热性疾病和产奶量减少,并可诱发胎儿先天畸形,这对全球牲畜健康构成重大关注。因此,迫切需要快速、现场适应性强的诊断方法。在本研究中,我们开发了一种 SBV 可视化核酸检测方法,将逆转录重组酶辅助扩增 (RT-RAA) 与 CRISPR/Cas12a 系统相结合,针对 SBV S 基因的保守区域。经过系统优化反应条件后,检测在 50 分钟内完成,SBV-S 质粒的灵敏度为 8.6 个拷贝/μL,RNA 转录本的灵敏度为 8.6 × 10 1 个拷贝/μL。该检测显示出高特异性,未观察到针对一组相关病原体的交叉反应,包括首尔正汉坦病毒(SEOV)、传染性牛鼻气管炎病毒(IBRV)、裂谷热病毒(RVFV)、克里米亚-刚果出血热病毒(CCHFV)和牛病毒性腹泻病毒(BVDV)。当使用模拟临床样本进行评估时,该方法的灵敏度优于传统的实时荧光逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-qPCR)。重要的是,整个反应以单闭管形式进行,显着降低了交叉污染和假阳性结果的风险。总之,该方法在检测 SBV-S 质粒掺入鼻拭子样本方面表现出良好的分析性能,并有望进一步进行临床验证,尽管其在真实临床标本中的诊断效用仍有待在未来的研究中得到证实。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 施马伦贝格病毒 (SBV) 会导致发热性疾病、成年反刍动物产奶量减少以及胎儿先天畸形,对全球牲畜健康构成重大威胁。迫切需要快速、适用于现场的诊断方法来解决这种新出现的虫媒病毒疾病。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究通过将逆转录重组酶辅助扩增 (RT-RAA) 与 CRISPR/Cas12a 系统相结合,开发了一种 SBV 可视化核酸检测方法,针对 SBV S 基因的保守区域。使用质粒和 RNA 转录标准品以及模拟临床样本对该测定进行了优化和评估。
analysis_zh.methods: 该测定针对 SBV S 基因的保守区域,并针对反应条件进行了优化,可在 50 分钟内完成。SBV-S 质粒的灵敏度确定为 8.6 拷贝/μL,RNA 转录本的灵敏度确定为 8.6 × 10^1 拷贝/μL。针对首尔正汉坦病毒 (SEOV)、传染性牛鼻气管炎病毒 (IBRV)、裂谷热病毒 (RVFV)、克里米亚-刚果出血热病毒 (CCHFV) 和牛病毒性腹泻病毒 (BVDV) 等一组病毒进行特异性评估,未观察到交叉反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该测定对 SBV-S 质粒的灵敏度为 8.6 拷贝/μL,对 RNA 转录本的灵敏度为 8.6 × 10^1 拷贝/μL,并且与测试的病原体组没有交叉反应。在模拟临床样本中,该检测的灵敏度超过了传统 RT-qPCR。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将该测定解释为证明了 SBV 检测的良好分析性能,强调其单一闭管形式可降低交叉污染风险。新颖之处在于 RT-RAA 与 CRISPR/Cas12a 的简化集成,可快速、直观地检测 SBV。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该测定可以实现快速、可现场部署的 SBV 检测,支持牲畜疾病 监测 和 暴发 应对。其闭管形式和对 RT-qPCR 的卓越敏感性表明在资源有限的环境中改善诊断工作流程的潜力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告真实临床标本的诊断验证,限制了直接的临床适用性。虽然分析性能很强,但缺乏现场测试会导致证据强度中等,直到完成进一步验证。

news.content: Social Media Links Facebook Twitter Instagram YouTube Rss Podcast whatsapp Search Close Start Date to End Date Select Type Select Type News Listen News Regional Bulletins Bulletins Detail News Programmes Special Programs Mann ki Baat From Archives Circulars RTI Replies Vacancies Regional Units Detail Download Mobile App Language Selection Englishहिन्दीमराठीગુજરાતીUrduDogriAssameseRajasthaniবাংলা Menu News On AIR International Regional News Business Sports Miscellaneous Archives Audios: News & Current Affairs Transcripts News in Regional Languages (Audios & Text) Text Archive Search Listen News Morning News Mann Ki Baat Screen Reader Access Transcript summary Play Audio Morning News Home International Hantavirus outbreak forces cruise passengers to leave ship at St Helena News On AIR | May 7, 2026 5:13 PM Hantavirus outbreak forces cruise passengers to leave ship at St Helena Around 40 passengers from a cruise ship hit by a deadly hantavirus outbreak disembarked at the remote South Atlantic island of St Helena last month without contact tracing, nearly two weeks after the first passenger died on board. The Dutch Foreign Ministry has confirmed the number. It comes as international authorities intensify efforts to contain a rare outbreak of deadly disease linked to the Andes strain of hantavirus after three people who were aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius have died since it set sail from Argentina a month ago. The Dutch-flagged expedition vessel, carrying around 150 passengers and crew from 23 different countries, is now sailing towards Spain’s Canary Islands under strict precautionary measures after being anchored for three days near Cape Verde, an archipelago nation off the West African coast. The ship operator company, Oceanwide Expeditions, had previously said the body of the Dutch man who died on the 11th of April was taken off the ship at the island of St Helena, where his wife also disembarked. She then flew to South Africa and died there. The company had not previously acknowledged that dozens more people left the ship at that time. The company said the people who left the ship to return to their home countries were of at least 12 different nationalities. Meanwhile, two passengers in serious condition have arrived in the Netherlands for treatment after being evacuated from the cruise ship. A third passenger, reported to be in stable condition, remains aboard a delayed evacuation flight. The three suspected hantavirus patients of British, Dutch and German nationalities were transferred by medical evacuation teams in full hazmat gear, including respirators, gowns and face shields, from the cruise ship into specialised air ambulances near Amsterdam and Cape Verde this week. The World Health Organisation said the outbreak likely involves the Andes strain of hantavirus – the only known strain capable of limited human-to-human transmission through close contact. Authorities in Europe, South Africa and Argentina are continuing contact tracing, quarantine planning and laboratory testing to contain the outbreak. Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome is usually transmitted through inhalation of aerosolised rodent urine, saliva or droppings. However, the Andes strain circulating in parts of Argentina and Chile has previously shown limited person-to-person transmission, particularly among close household contacts. news.content: Feedback | Friday, August 07, 2026 Skip Navigation DD News Menu Search Live Radio HI Top Stories National International Mann ki Baat Education Health Business & Economy Science & Tech Sports Commonwealth Environment Opinion Your browser does not support Javascript Tweets by DDNewslive Your browser does not support Javascript Home Top Stories What is the hantavirus that killed three cruise ship passengers? 04/05/26 | 9:55 am | hantavirus | netharland Share Your browser does not support JavaScript What is the hantavirus that killed three cruise ship passengers? Three people have died and three are ill after a Netherlands-based cruise ship was hit by a suspected outbreak of hantavirus, authorities and media reports said on Sunday. Here is information about the virus. SPREAD BY RODENTS Hantavirus is primarily spread by rodents but can be transmitted between people in rare cases, according to the World Health Organization. People most typically become infected when virus in rodent droppings, saliva and urine becomes airborne, such as when areas where rats and mice have nested are swept out. According to The Lancet medical journal, the name comes from the Hantan River area of South Korea, where the virus was identified in the 1970s. CAN BE FATAL Hantavirus is a family of viruses that cause two illnesses, one that primarily affects the lungs and the other that attacks the kidneys. The first gets the most attention because it has a high fatality rate of about 40%. Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, the respiratory illness, is most commonly found in North and South America. According to the Canadian government, about 200 cases of hantavirus pulmonary illness occur each year worldwide. Concert pianist Betsy Arakawa, wife of actor Gene Hackman, died from hantavirus pulmonary syndrome in New Mexico in 2025, according to autopsy results. SYMPTOMS Hantavirus usually begins with flu-like symptoms, such as fatigue and fever, one to eight weeks after exposure, according to the CDC. Four to 10 days later, coughing, shortness of breath and fluid in the lungs appear. Diagnosis in the first 72 hours of infection is difficult, the CDC says, so symptoms can easily be mistaken for flu. TREATMENT There is no specific therapy for hantavirus infection, so treatment focuses on supportive care including rest and fluids. Patients may need breathing support such as a ventilator. PREVENTION Experts say exposure to hantavirus can be minimized by deterring and eliminating rodents from areas where people are. Avoid vacuuming or sweeping dried droppings, which can aerosolize the virus. Three people have died and three are ill after a Netherlands-based cruise ship was hit by a suspected outbreak of hantavirus, authorities and media reports said on Sunday. Here is information about the virus. SPREAD BY RODENTS Hantavirus is primarily spread by rodents but can be transmitted between people in rare cases, according to the World Health Organization. People most typically become infected when virus in rodent droppings, saliva and urine becomes airborne, such as when areas where rats and mice have nested are swept out. According to The Lancet medical journal, the name comes from the Hantan River area of South Korea, where the virus was identified in the 1970s. CAN BE FATAL Hantavirus is a family of viruses that cause two illnesses, one that primarily affects the lungs and the other that attacks the kidneys. The first gets the most attention because it has a high fatality rate of about 40%. Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, the respiratory illness, is most commonly found in North and South America. According to the Canadian government, about 200 cases of hantavirus pulmonary illness occur each year worldwide. Concert pianist Betsy Arakawa, wife of actor Gene Hackman, died from hantavirus pulmonary syndrome in New Mexico in 2025, according to autopsy results. SYMPTOMS Hantavirus usually begins with flu-like symptoms, such as fatigue and fever, one to eight weeks after exposure, according to the CDC. Four to 10 days later, coughing, shortness of breath and fluid in the lungs appear. Diagnosis in the first 72 hours of infection is difficult, the CDC says, so symptoms can easily be mistaken for flu. TREATMENT There is no specific therapy for hantavirus infection, so treatment focuses on supportive care including rest and fluids. Patients may need breathing support such as a ventilator. PREVENTION Experts say exposure to hantavirus can be minimized by deterring and eliminating rodents from areas where people are. Avoid vacuuming or sweeping dried droppings, which can aerosolize the virus. news.content_title: Hantavirus explained: from hamsters to human trials
news.content: On 3 May 2026, the World Health Organisation (WHO) issued an alert regarding a possible outbreak of hantavirus on board a Dutch cruise ship travelling from Ushuaia, Argentina, to Cape Verde. It’s not extraordinary for a cruise ship to be afflicted by an infectious disease. However, this is the first instance of a hantavirus outbreak, and circumstances have led public health officials to observe the situation closely. But what do we know about the disease ? Hantaviruses are zoonotic viruses found on every continent, transmitted primarily through indirect contact with infected rodents. Over 50 hantavirus species have been identified, and an estimated 100,000 human infections occur each year, predominantly in Asia and Europe. Hantavirus infections can cause two life-threatening syndromes: haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (fatality rate 1–15%) and severe acute cardiopulmonary syndrome with respiratory and cardiac failure (fatality rate 30–60%). There are currently no licensed vaccines or treatments. A major obstacle to developing hantavirus treatments is the lack of animal models that accurately reproduce human disease: rodents, the natural reservoir, typically carry the virus for life with minimal symptoms, making them poor models for studying how the infection harms people. A breakthrough Syrian hamster model that mimics hantavirus pulmonary syndrome in humans has enabled the development of vaccines for Andes, Hantaan, and Puumala hantaviruses, which have now entered Phase I human clinical trials, alongside an antibody-based treatment produced using genetically modified cows. A zoonotic pathogen found on every continent The first clinical description of a hantavirus disease dates back to the Korean War (1950–1953), during which more than 3,000 soldiers fell ill. It wasn’t until 1978 that the causative agent was first described by Korean researchers Lee et al ., in the lungs of its natural reservoir, the striped field mouse. The virus was named after the Hantaan River, which lies on the border between North and South Korea. Today, hantaviruses are understood to belong to a large group of viruses that are found on every continent. More than 50 viral species have been identified across the globe, all of which are zoonotic – that is, transmitted by animals. These are mainly wild rodents (rats, voles, field mice) and, more rarely, insectivorous rodents ( moles , shrews ) and bats . Multiple hantaviruses such as Hantaan virus, Seoul virus, Dobrava-Belgrade virus, Puumala virus, Andes virus, and Sin Nombre virus are highly pathogenic to humans. Transmission to humans mainly occurs through indirect contact (saliva, urine, faeces) of asymptomatic infected rodents (referred to as “reservoir” animals) and, more rarely, through direct contact or bites. Human-to-human transmission is rare and appears to involve only the Andes hantavirus – the one that was identified on the cruise ship. Around 100,000 cases of hantavirus infections are estimated to occur each year, mainly in Asia and Europe. About 90% of all the documented cases worldwide occur in China but Europe totals some 10,000 cases every year in Finland, Germany, Belgium, France, UK, Poland, and the Balkans. In the Americas, the numbers are much lower with a total of eight countries (Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Chile, Panama, Paraguay, the USA and Uruguay) reporting only 229 cases and 59 deaths in 2025 . However, these numbers are growing every year. Hantaviruses represent a significant and emerging global public health threat, with a devastating effect on human lives and a high mortality rate. A multi-faceted viral infection When they affect humans, hantaviruses can cause infections of varying severity. Two types of syndrome may then be observed: haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, fatal in 1% to 15% of cases, and severe acute cardiopulmonary syndrome with respiratory and cardiac failure, with a fatality rate of around 30% to 60%. Both syndromes can be caused by the same viral species. However, renal and hepatic syndrome is more commonly found in European and Asian hantaviruses (commonly referred to as “Old World” hantaviruses), while the more dangerous pulmonary syndrome is more commonly observed in American hantaviruses (or “New World” hantaviruses). Unfortunately, there are currently no licensed treatments or vaccines available to combat hantaviruses. Hantavirus infections are dealt with mostly by managing the symptoms and providing supporting care. The development of vaccines and antivirals remains critical for mitigating hantaviral infections and their impact on public health. However, the mechanisms of pathogenesis are still poorly defined . A better understanding of the virus biology is urgently required, including understanding how infection within rodent carrier populations leads to the emergence of human pathogens and why some of these viruses are able to subvert immune defences and establish high burden disease in humans. These answers will rely on basic research conducted, in part, in animals. There is still a lot we don’t know about hantaviruses Medical countermeasures that could held dissipate the threat hantaviruses pose to human populations will require a better understanding of the virus and how it works. This research calls for animal models that faithfully recapitulate the human disease caused by the viral infection. Unfortunately, there are no small animal models that fully recapitulate human haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) disease . Rodents seem to contract persistent, lifelong infection with minimal symptoms, which allows for a long-term maintenance of the pathogen within the host population , but doesn’t fully reflect what happens in humans. One of the main reasons we struggle to develop protective or therapeutic options for humans, is the lack of good animal disease models to support the research . Novel antivirals are being tested , some showing promising results , but in vivo testing is often limited to the Andes variant and animal models lacking human-like disease. Without a representative model, it is difficult to investigate potential new drugs. Several attempts have been made to establish an animal model for hantavirus-like diseases that reflects the human disease. Initial efforts to create a hantavirus nonhuman primate (NHP) disease model were largely unsuccessful . Recently, however, the first hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) monkey model was described. It emulates HPS human disease but is a logistically complex model, requiring the monkeys to be infected via a deer mouse vector. Rodent models have also been developed more or less successfully. Early pathogenicity studies examined infection in suckling mice and rats with a naturally low immune system, but this often resulted in high lethality. Some immunodeficient mouse models also exhibited some of the human-like symptoms of infection. Despite being limited as pathogenesis (natural disease) models, mice are used extensively in evaluation of vaccine immunogenicity and protective efficacy . The first real breakthrough was the development of a model for the Andes virus in Syrian hamsters . An immunocompromised version of this model was later adapted to the Sin Nombre virus (SNV). Immunosuppressed Syrian hamsters were infected with various New World hantavirus strains , resulting in an acute disease that mimicked hantavirus pulmonary syndrome in humans. The hamster model has also been used to examine the pathogenesis of hantaviruses and evaluate several vaccines . Interviewed by Nature , virologist Jay Hooper explained that “a key advance of our team has been developing hamster models of a lethal disease very similar to human hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. This provides a realistic animal model to test vaccines and therapeutics.” Using this model, the team developed vaccines for Andes virus, Hantaan and Puumala hantaviruses that have now reached Phase I human clinical trials. The research team is also developing an antibody-based treatment to combat the Andes virus and three other hantaviruses, that is produced using genetically modified cows. As animal models get better at reproducing the viral infection in human, the search for new therapeutics and vaccines is likely to become more successful. These answers will rely on basic research conducted, in part, in animals. There is still a lot we don’t know about hantaviruses Medical countermeasures that could held dissipate the threat hantaviruses pose to human populations will require a better understanding of the virus and how it works. This research calls for animal models that faithfully recapitulate the human disease caused by the viral infection. Unfortunately, there are no small animal models that fully recapitulate human haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) disease . Rodents seem to contract persistent, lifelong infection with minimal symptoms, which allows for a long-term maintenance of the pathogen within the host population , but doesn’t fully reflect what happens in humans. One of the main reasons we struggle to develop protective or therapeutic options for humans, is the lack of good animal disease models to support the research . Novel antivirals are being tested , some showing promising results , but in vivo testing is often limited to the Andes variant and animal models lacking human-like disease. Without a representative model, it is difficult to investigate potential new drugs. Several attempts have been made to establish an animal model for hantavirus-like diseases that reflects the human disease. Initial efforts to create a hantavirus nonhuman primate (NHP) disease model were largely unsuccessful . Recently, however, the first hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) monkey model was described. It emulates HPS human disease but is a logistically complex model, requiring the monkeys to be infected via a deer mouse vector. Rodent models have also been developed more or less successfully. Early pathogenicity studies examined infection in suckling mice and rats with a naturally low immune system, but this often resulted in high lethality. Some immunodeficient mouse models also exhibited some of the human-like symptoms of infection. Despite being limited as pathogenesis (natural disease) models, mice are used extensively in evaluation of vaccine immunogenicity and protective efficacy . The first real breakthrough was the development of a model for the Andes virus in Syrian hamsters . An immunocompromised version of this model was later adapted to the Sin Nombre virus (SNV). Immunosuppressed Syrian hamsters were infected with various New World hantavirus strains , resulting in an acute disease that mimicked hantavirus pulmonary syndrome in humans. The hamster model has also been used to examine the pathogenesis of hantaviruses and evaluate several vaccines . Interviewed by Nature , virologist Jay Hooper explained that “a key advance of our team has been developing hamster models of a lethal disease very similar to human hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. This provides a realistic animal model to test vaccines and therapeutics.” Using this model, the team developed vaccines for Andes virus, Hantaan and Puumala hantaviruses that have now reached Phase I human clinical trials. The research team is also developing an antibody-based treatment to combat the Andes virus and three other hantaviruses, that is produced using genetically modified cows. As animal models get better at reproducing the viral infection in human, the search for new therapeutics and vaccines is likely to become more successful. analysis.brief_en: On 3 May 2026, the World Health Organisation (WHO) issued an alert about a possible hantavirus outbreak on a Dutch cruise ship traveling from Ushuaia, Argentina, to Cape Verde. This is the first reported hantavirus outbreak, prompting close monitoring by public health officials. Hantaviruses are zoonotic, found on every continent, and primarily transmitted through indirect contact with infected rodents. They can cause two severe syndromes: haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), with a fatality rate of 1–15%, and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), with a fatality rate of 30–60%. Over 50 species have been identified, with an estimated 100,000 human infections annually, mostly in Asia and Europe. In the Americas, 229 cases and 59 deaths were reported in 2025. Currently, no licensed vaccines or treatments exist. However, a breakthrough Syrian hamster model has enabled Phase I clinical trials for vaccines targeting Andes, Hantaan, and Puumala hantaviruses, alongside an antibody-based treatment developed using genetically modified cows. The lack of effective animal models has hindered treatment development, but recent advances in research offer hope for future interventions.
